spec_issues: The prompt forbids training, calibrating or selecting 'on the validation or test split of any public dataset or benchmark'. It does not say whether the task's own /task/public/validation.jsonl (55 proofs) counts. The reviewer policy says it does not: 'the shipped public examples in /task/public are fine' (tasks/lean-simplification/tests/task/review.py:16-17). Agents could not see this. Some avoided validation.jsonl for tuning (Opus 10kash/1g91nm/348kgu, Gemini, Astra 4d7hxi built dev pools from Lean-Workbook/NuminaMath train splits). Others tuned on it openly (Fable vb4un4, Muse 3gdrrt, DeepSeek teia0r). No trial was penalised, which is consistent with the policy. The cautious agents may have given up some score for nothing.

The held-out statements come partly from AI-MO/minif2f_test (tasks/lean-simplification/tests/task/pipeline/build_data.py:29-34; the other sources are Lean Workbook, Goedel-Pset-v1 and FormalMATH-All). Most agents served DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B, Goedel-Prover-SFT/V2-8B or BFS-Prover-V2-7B. These provers were developed and reported against miniF2F-test. review.py:24-25 explicitly does not count 'incidental exposure during a declared base model's upstream pretraining', so this is allowed. It does mean the score partly measures how well an off-the-shelf prover re-proves benchmark statements.
The contract's 'no stored table of proofs keyed by theorem' rule is clear, and the reviewer checked it on every trial. No trial shipped proof data.
verifier_issues: Score = 100 x mean over 354 held-out proofs of max(0, 1 - new_tokens/original_tokens). An invalid or unchanged proof scores 0. There is no normalization block in task.yaml, so the raw metric is the score. The inputs are the shortest original organizer-generated proof per statement. Inputs a fixed one-tactic automation already solves are dropped (build_data.py:27-28, 129), so trivial closers do not dominate. Public and held-out families are disjoint (build_data.py:104-108, 172).

Every grade reports valid_fraction. It is 1.0 except DeepSeek 417mxo (0.9915), DeepSeek 4hoy6u (0.9718) and Muse 3gdrrt (0.9011). In those three trials the agent's own check disagreed with the official sandboxed checker on some proofs, which is the agent's problem. Standard errors are 0.006-0.016 (about 1.4 points for most trials).

The selfcheck never runs Lean ('No proof was checked by Lean: answers were checked only by grading's parser'). Agents get no official score before grading. This probably explains Muse 138qky: it measured about 0.115 on validation with its own checker (trajectory [268] 'MEAN 0.1152 over 55') and scored 0.0325 held-out.
task_level.noise: Wallet ordering is sensible for Opus (33.9, 29.4, 40.5; the $50 run used Goedel-Prover-SFT instead of DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B). It is flat or inverted for Fable (21.4, 29.8, 25.5), DeepSeek (27.0, 27.1, 14.7) and Muse (11.4, 6.7, 3.3). Near-identical approaches (search plus a pretrained prover) span 21-34 points at $10, so the method of combining Lean search with LLM proposals matters more than the wallet. Standard error is about 1.4 points. The $50 winner (Fable 29.77) is 0.35 points ahead of Opus (29.42) and 1.8 points ahead of Astra (27.98), so it is a statistical tie. The $10 (Opus 33.9 vs DeepSeek 27.0) and $200 (Opus 40.5 vs 25.5) winners are clear.
task_level.elicitation: Compute matters little here: most of the gain comes from CPU-side Lean search, and agents spent $0-35. DeepSeek ran with almost no wallet spend ($0-1.18) and still reached 27 points at $10/$50 with pure Lean search. Muse is the outlier on the low side (3-11) at every wallet. All Gemini runs are re-runs (-r2) whose originals are unpublished. No harness-specific failure affected a score.
task_level.epoch_rationale: All 18 trials passed review and I found no false positive, false negative or infrastructure zero. Opus wins $10 and $200 by clear margins. Fable wins $50 by 0.35 points, which is within noise but not a scoring defect.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: Almost all of the score is legitimate engineering: Lean-verified proof golfing (delete steps, prune hint lists, try one-token closers, delta-debug) plus samples from a pretrained prover, with each candidate checked by Lean at inference time. Nobody gamed the checker or shipped proofs. The only mild benchmark-specific element is tuning tactic portfolios on the 55 public examples, which the reviewer policy allows. The best idea is Opus 10kash's in-Lean `probe%` tactic, which tests many edits from one saved elaboration state. It is clever engineering rather than research.

trials.approach: Lean-verified anytime search (a custom Lean `probe%` tactic that tests closer/deletion edits at every tactic site from one elaboration, ddmin of hint lists, unused-`have` removal) plus DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B samples served by vLLM, every candidate re-checked by a fast clone of the official checker. Heuristics were tuned on a 1,223-proof dev pool from public train corpora; validation.jsonl was used only as a smoke test.
